items.description: ComAfrica is a consumer-goods manufacturer based in Icon Industrial Park, Sunderland Ridge, producing personal care and household products distributed across Sub-Saharan Africa and sold through a wholesale division. Its product range is built around three in-house brands: Crez, BioFresh and Veerox. Under the Crez name, the company makes a petroleum jelly line available in seven variants, formulated to repair and relieve dry skin, alongside a hand and body cream sold in four variants that uses a rich formulation designed to lock in moisture and leave a long-lasting scent. The BioFresh brand covers household cleaning products, including a Pine-Gel that doubles as a detergent, deodoriser and degreaser for cleaning surfaces while neutralising odours, and a concentrated lemon-scented dishwashing liquid formulated to cut through grease. The company also produces a multi-purpose cleaner strong enough to cut through grease and grime without heavy scrubbing, and a mosquito repellent suitable for the whole family. ComAfrica describes itself as a proudly African company aiming to grow its footprint across the continent.

Comcor Engineering, founded in 2008 and based in Boardwalk Office Park, Faerie Glen, provides electrical, instrumentation and control systems engineering to the industrial process sector. The company offers a full scope of engineering services covering design, procurement, construction and commissioning of EC&I systems for industrial process plants, and is experienced across the complete project life cycle, from basic engineering design through to commissioning and hand-over. It has completed numerous large and small projects on both green-field and brown-field bases, and also provides professional services during the feasibility-study and cost-estimate phases of projects. Comcor's work spans the mining and minerals-processing, energy and power, chemical-processing and infrastructure sectors, including airport projects. Its client base includes Impala Platinum, a leading producer of platinum group metals, the global energy company ENGIE, and ASP Isotopes, a specialist in isotope-enrichment technology for the medical, semiconductor and green-energy sectors.

CosultX, based in Rietvalleirand, Pretoria, was founded by a father-and-son team to address the growing fire risk posed by lithium batteries. The company distributes fire extinguishers and automated suppression systems designed specifically for lithium battery incidents, serving customers in both Pretoria and Johannesburg. Its extinguishing technology works through three mechanisms: a temperature-reduction stage that rapidly cools overheating lithium batteries to prevent thermal runaway, an oxygen-suppression stage that smothers the fire by cutting off its oxygen supply, and a reignition-prevention stage that seals the battery in a specialised gel to stop the fire restarting. CosultX states that all of its products are rigorously tested to ensure reliable performance when needed. The company positions itself as a specialist distributor focused on lithium battery fire safety specifically, rather than general fire-safety equipment, reflecting the increased risk that lithium batteries present in environments that rely on them.

Cotton S A is the representative body for South Africa's cotton industry, based in Salieshoek, Pretoria. It provides information on the history of cotton, production cycles and growing areas, as well as grading and classification services covering quality control, training and textile testing. The organisation administers the Cotton Mark, a certification applied to cotton products, and publishes industry reports, statistics and contact information covering the sector from farm to fashion. Cotton S A also explains the pricing arrangements used in the local industry: most South African cotton is sold through marketing pools, where a ginner combines multiple producers' cotton into larger lots to negotiate better prices than individual farmers could achieve alone. Farmers typically receive an upfront cash payment based on the amount of cotton placed in the pool, with further proceeds distributed once the pooled cotton is sold to merchants or textile mills, adjusted for quality against a base standard.

Courier Direct is a courier company based at Samrand Business Park in Centurion, serving the logistics industry with same-day, express and domestic eCommerce parcel delivery. It offers a cost-effective and flexible courier service to both individual and corporate customers, adapting to each customer's requirements around collection and delivery times, locations and billing procedures. The company emphasises prompt response to collection requests, prompt delivery of shipments and prompt handling of customer queries. Courier Direct aims to be a customer's courier company of choice for parcel services, combining same-day and express shipping with eCommerce-focused courier solutions for online vendors. It accepts payment through a range of payment partners, and describes its growth in market share within the logistics sector as reflecting an evolving approach to meeting customer needs across domestic and corporate shipping.

Craftivo is a bespoke wooden furniture workshop based in Koedoespoort Industrial, Pretoria. The company designs and builds custom kitchens and cabinetry, bathroom vanities, and built-in cupboards and storage tailored to a client's space, from bedrooms to pantries. Its range also covers interior doors and cladding, display cabinets and occasional tables, themed children's bedrooms, and headboards and other bedroom furniture. Beyond furniture, Craftivo makes smaller wooden items such as beehives, laptop tables and serving boards, describing these as sustainably made. The business works with interior designers on trade projects and with homeowners on bespoke pieces built to a specified budget and decor style, and also manufactures furniture on a wholesale basis for retail outlets and online shops. In addition to new pieces, Craftivo offers furniture repairs, restoring existing items and fixing problems such as damaged cupboard doors.

Crema Café is a coffee shop in Elardus Park that was opened by Collage Community Church as a space for people in the local community to connect with each other. The café positions coffee as something that inspires work and brings people together, offering both an in-shop menu and an online menu for customers. Its focus is on serving quality coffee in a welcoming environment where visitors can work or socialise over a cup. The business describes its purpose in simple terms: creating a space where coffee becomes the common ground that draws people into conversation and community. Crema Café operates from premises at the corner of Gypsum and Hornblend Streets in Elardus Park, serving the surrounding Pretoria community during the week and on Sundays.

CUM Books is a Christian bookstore chain with a branch in Menlyn Retail Park, Newlands, Pretoria. The store sells Bibles across a wide range of translations, including the Amplified Bible, Christian Standard Bible, English Standard Version, King James Version, The Message, New American Standard, New English Translation, New International Version, New King James Version and New Living Translation, available in both English and Afrikaans. Beyond Bibles, CUM Books stocks journals and notebooks, journaling and creative Bibles, Bible studies, Bible bags and book covers, general stationery, home and kitchen items, and a range of Christian-themed gifts. The chain also carries daily planners and diaries, including annual and multi-month formats aimed at different readers. As a specialist Christian retailer, CUM Books positions its Menlyn branch within a national network of stores focused on faith-based reading material, devotional products and related homeware and stationery.

Design n Touch is a bespoke software development company based in Queenswood, Pretoria, building AI-driven web and mobile applications for businesses. The company focuses on creating software that goes beyond aesthetics, aiming to improve efficiency and open new opportunities for its clients through practical, results-driven applications. Its team describes itself as African developers building solutions designed around the specific challenges faced across the African continent, combining local market knowledge with current technology. Design n Touch follows an Agile approach to software delivery and takes a security-first stance, applying security-centric practices across all the software products it develops for customers. Rather than offering off-the-shelf packages, the company tailors each project to a client's particular needs, positioning itself as a provider of bespoke software solutions built around current advances in development technology.

Services cover residential DStv support, including fault-finding across houses, apartments and multi-room installations, as well as reception and signal-quality checks.
